steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Inspect the source, effective configuration, launch script,
metrics, rollouts, debug probes and frozen evidence. Connect any unusual
implementation to observed behavior rather than treating it as causal by
appearance alone.

Do not launch training, use the network, or modify the historical snapshot.
Write one concise diagnosis to `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md`. State the
verdict, concrete root cause and causal evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms; do not implement a fix.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-pissa_residual_reference}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}

RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug

printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"

cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=4 \
  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
  data.max_response_length=32 \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=2026 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.05 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.fsdp_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode=async \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.35 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=512 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs=16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.temperature=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False \
  reward_model.reward_manager=naive \
  trainer.logger='[console,wandb,file]' \
  trainer.project_name=AutoRLBench-Minimal-RL \
  trainer.experiment_name="${RUN_NAME}" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_epochs=4 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=4 \
  trainer.default_local_dir="${LOG_DIR}/checkpoints-disabled" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations" \
  trainer.log_val_generations=4 \
  +trainer.log_base_model_kl=True \
  +trainer.log_final_policy_health=True \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_DIR}/train.log"

- `val-health/base_reference_consistency`: 0.0458 — very low. `base_reference_mae`: 3.08. Actor vs rollout policy: mae 0.11, agreement 0.89.

So the "base model" KL vs reference is wrong — the reference model likely isn't the intended base. The setup uses PiSSA residual base + LoRA adapter. In PiSSA, training should have residual_base as frozen base + trainable LoRA on top, and reference KL should be computed against... The bundle manifest might describe. Check debug probes and manifest.

# Diagnosis: PiSSA residual-base RL run (verl, qwen2.5-0.5b, tiny-gsm8k)

## Verdict
The core training loop (rollout → advantage → GRPO policy update → rollout sync) is functioning
(gradients flow, rewards occur, actor↔rollout stay in sync), but the run is **unhealthy** in one
specific respect: the PiSSA "base-model KL" bookkeeping is broken. The frozen SVD reference adapter
that is supposed to reproduce the original pretrained base model never does, so every
`actor/base_model_kl*` metric — and the health gate built on it — reports garbage.

## Evidence
- Health check at step 4: `val-health/base_reference_mae = 3.08` →
  `base_reference_consistency = 0.046` (≈0). This metric directly compares
  `compute_base_ref_log_prob` (production base-ref) against
  `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` (independent ground truth via
  `_svd_init_adapter_ctx`, which activates the frozen `_base_ref` adapter containing the saved
  initial PiSSA factors over the residual base — i.e. true `W_orig`). A 3.08 nats/token divergence
  means the production path is **not** scoring the original base model.
- Debug probes confirm the production base-ref is much too harsh: base_ref mean logprob −17.3 vs
  policy old −19.4 (`actor_update.rank0.json`, `pre_update.rank0.json`), and the reported
  `actor/base_model_kl` is a nonsensical **−4.0 to −4.9** every step. A KL of the initial PiSSA
  policy against its own base should be ≈ 0 at step 0; a large *negative* value is impossible for a
  real KL and proves the two logprob streams come from different models.
- Contrast: `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement = 0.89` and rollout↔training logprob
  Pearson ≈ 0.99 — so policy plumbing is fine. The defect is isolated to the base-reference path.

## Root cause
In `verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py`, `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor()` handles the SVD-init
(PiSSA residual-base) case identically to plain LoRA: it sets `is_lora=True`, which makes
`compute_log_prob` wrap the forward in `actor_module.disable_adapter()`. With a residual base,
disabling the adapter exposes `W_res` — **not** the original pretrained model `W_orig = W_res +
BA`. The correct SVD path (`_svd_init_adapter_ctx`, switching to the frozen `_base_ref` adapter so
`W_res + B₀A₀ = W_orig`) is implemented and is exactly what the health check uses as "expected",
but it is never invoked in the production path: neither `compute_ref_log_prob` (used for
`ref_log_prob` in the KL loss) nor the `log_base_model_kl` branch of `update_actor` uses it.
The `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` block in `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` is therefore dead code on
the branch that matters — the function passes `is_lora=True` instead of switching adapters.

## Consequences (symptoms, not causes)
1. **Wrong KL regularizer target**: with `use_kl_loss=True`, `ref_log_prob` is computed via
   `compute_ref_log_prob` → the same broken path, so the KL loss anchors the adapter to the
   *residual base* `W_res` instead of the true base `W_orig`. The persistent `actor/kl_loss`
   ≈ 0.76–0.98 (vs an expected ≈0 for a PiSSA init at step 0) is the same misreference seen from
   the loss side.
2. **Misleading diagnostics**: `actor/base_model_kl ≈ −4.x` and `base_model_kl_pre_update ≈ −4.x`
   are artifacts of comparing the policy against `W_res`, not evidence of policy collapse.
3. The PiSSA factorization itself is loaded correctly (adapter init forced to `False`, initial
   factors saved, rollout sync uses `svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights` on first sync) —
   the bug is only in reference/base logprob computation, not in the trained weights.

## Bottom line
Training is numerically stable and learning signal exists, but the KL-to-base objective and all
base-model KL metrics are computed against the wrong reference (`W_res` instead of `W_orig`) because
the SVD-init base-ref path uses `disable_adapter()` instead of the frozen `_base_ref` adapter that
`_svd_init_adapter_ctx` already provides. This is the root cause; the negative KL values and the
~0 `base_reference_consistency` are its symptoms.
